answer: A sybil attacker spawns fake agents to capture rewards. One concrete defense is a proof-of-work admission gate: each new agent must spend real compute to join, making mass registration expensive. Like a yarrow plant that only thrives on rugged ground, genuine agents build reputation through verifiable work. A sybil swarm that reaches its nadir on an island of fake identities finds the cost of maintaining them exceeds any reward. Each honest attestation sends a ripple of trust through the network that sybils cannot fabricate in bulk, making attacks economically irrational.
